tasks.title: Smoke the rebased app on port 30142 with the fork checklist
tasks.detail:
Goal: prove at runtime what typecheck cannot — that the fork features and the new upstream features both work.
Files: none; the dev server writes only to worktree-local .next/.
Contract: run from /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream with `PI_WEB_*` env left default, on port 30142 so the live app on 4201 is untouched. Checklist (each item observed, not assumed):
1. App boots; sidebar shows project groups and the Files tab (upstream) and a pinned section once a session is pinned (fork).
2. `POST /api/sessions/pinned` round-trips and survives a page reload.
3. Open a text file, edit, save — `PUT /api/files/...` returns a new revision; a stale `baseRevision` returns 409.
4. A package with `piWeb.panels` renders in its right-panel tab next to the subagent viewer tab.
5. `PI_WEB_EXTENSION_MODE=tui` is honoured (extension sees `ctx.mode === "tui"`), and an extension with a custom component still renders.
6. A `sudo` command in the bash tool raises the browser password prompt and the command succeeds with the answer.
7. MCP settings pane from upstream opens and lists servers (no connection required).
Steps:
1. `npm run dev` in the worktree (port 30141 default is taken by nothing; confirm 30142 is free and start with the port flag if needed).
2. Walk the checklist, capturing the failing item verbatim if something breaks; fix in the owning file and re-run.
3. Stop the dev server; do not delete .next while debugging without a fresh restart.
Verify: every checklist item observed working, with the evidence (HTTP status, screenshot or log line) in progress.
Done when: the checklist passes end to end and no dev server is left running.

tasks.title: Write the fork documentation and deploy runbook
tasks.detail:
Goal: leave the fork in a state where the next person knows what was rebased and how to deploy it.
Files: the two documentation files only.
Contract: `LOCAL-CHANGES.md` keeps its attribution block (unofficial fork, upstream link, MIT, `origin`/`upstream` remotes) and gains: the new base tag, the per-hop tags (`fork-next-v0.10.0`, `fork-next-v0.11.1`, `fork-next-v0.12.2`), the branch/worktree layout (`custom` = deploy, `custom-next` = rebased), a feature-to-commit mapping, and the deploy steps. `AGENTS.md` fork sections must describe the code as it is after the rebase (new sidebar files, new panel layout), not the pre-rebase layout.
Steps:
1. Rewrite the fork sections of `LOCAL-CHANGES.md` for base v0.12.2.
2. Correct the `AGENTS.md` paragraphs that name files upstream renamed or split.
3. Add a "Promote custom-next to custom" runbook: verify `git -C /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web status` clean, migrate the branch (fast-forward `custom` to `custom-next`), then `npm install && npm run build` inside the main checkout and `pm2 restart pi-web-custom` — explicitly noting this interrupts any running agent session, so run it when idle.
Verify: `git grep -n 'v0\.9\.3' LOCAL-CHANGES.md AGENTS.md` returns only deliberate historical references; no documentation names a deleted file.
Done when: both documents describe the post-rebase fork and the runbook is explicit about the interruption risk.

tasks.title: Final audit: deploy branch untouched, fork delta clean
tasks.detail:
Goal: independent confirmation that nothing leaked into the deploy branch and the rebased delta contains only fork work.
Files: read-only audit; no writes.
Contract: three proofs are required — (a) `/home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web` is still on `custom` at 7092dba with a clean tree and the app on 4201 has the same PID family as before the work, (b) `git -C /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream log --oneline v0.12.2..custom-next` lists only fork commits (no upstream commit appears as a fork commit), (c) `git diff --stat v0.12.2..custom-next` contains no file that upstream owns exclusively and no lockfile churn beyond the fork's added dependencies.
Steps:
1. Run the three checks and paste the exact command output into progress.
2. Report any deviation as a defect with the file and commit that caused it.
Verify: all three checks pass verbatim; the audit output is in progress.
Done when: the audit is recorded and the branch is declared either ready or blocked with named defects.
